requirements.requirement: A nightly job on node1 pulls /srv/inventory/data from node2
requirements.summary: A cron job (/etc/cron.d/inventory-backup) runs /usr/local/sbin/inventory-backup.sh daily at 02:30 as root; crond confirmed active. The script SSHes to node2 and tars /srv/inventory/data over the connection. Manual execution succeeded and archive contents were extracted and verified to match the source files.

requirements.requirement: Dated archives are stored under /var/backups/inventory on node1
requirements.summary: Archive inventory-2026-09-03.tar.gz was created at /var/backups/inventory with a date-stamped filename; contents verified via tar listing and extraction to match source item_1.txt..item_3.txt.

requirements.requirement: Last 7 days of archives are retained; older archives are pruned
requirements.summary: Eight synthetic archives dated older than 7 days were all deleted on the next script run (via find -mtime pruning), while a synthetic archive dated exactly 5 days old was correctly retained, directly demonstrating the retention boundary in both directions.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node1 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/pipeline state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 45c22b1f... with crond/sshd active. Reboot was acknowledged, node became unreachable, then returned with a new boot_id (ecfabf1a...) confirmed both by executor commands and the fixed after-executor snapshot. Post-restart recovery showed crond/sshd active, cron file and prior archive intact, script checksum unchanged, and SSH connectivity to node2 restored.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node2 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/pipeline state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id bccb87ac... with sshd active and source data present. Reboot was acknowledged, node became unreachable, then returned with a new boot_id (d1f51986...) confirmed both by executor commands and the fixed after-executor snapshot. Post-restart recovery showed sshd active and source data intact, and a full end-to-end backup pipeline re-run from node1 succeeded after both restarts.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the backup task were directly demonstrated: a nightly cron-driven script pulls /srv/inventory/data from node2 to dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1, and 7-day retention was proven in both directions using synthetic aged files. The independently required provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently evidenced for both nodes, with pre-restart baselines, acknowledged reboots, changed boot identities cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and confirmed recovery of services, data, and the end-to-end backup pipeline. Operational hygiene is high — all test/setup mutations were either necessary and retained appropriately or fully cleaned up, with no residue, failed services, or exposure changes.
limitations: The source path /srv/inventory/data did not pre-exist on node2; the executor created placeholder data to make the pipeline testable. This is a reasonable interpretation of the task but means the evidence validates the mechanism on synthetic data rather than pre-existing production data.

Retention was validated using synthetic file timestamps (touch -d) rather than by observing 7+ real nightly cron runs, since the cron job had not yet fired at 02:30 during the observation window; this is standard for validating pruning logic but is not a live multi-day observation.

The cron schedule itself (02:30 nightly) was not observed actually firing under crond in this trace; its configuration and manual invocation are verified, but autonomous triggering was not directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's mutations are all clearly tied to the task or its verification. Creating source data on node2 (cmd-997cda444ae2439d) was necessary since /srv/inventory/data did not pre-exist and is required by the task contract; it remains as the legitimate data being backed up, not residue. Synthetic aged archives created to test 7-day retention (cmd-526c3b37d7734c59) were fully consumed/deleted by the retention logic itself in the very next script run (cmd-7a31f651a77a4976), and the synthetic 5-day-old retention-boundary file (cmd-60ca538f05194d52) was explicitly removed afterward (cmd-f395d0e83e884b50) — both bounded, low-risk, and fully cleaned up. The SSH keypair installation and known_hosts additions were necessary prerequisites for the backup pipeline. The two reboots were required by the provider-wide restart protocol and left only expected transient artifacts (/tmp/reboot.log, new systemd-private dirs tied to the new boot) with no failed services, no new listening sockets beyond the pre-existing set, and no package-health regressions per the after-executor snapshot. No unreverted, unnecessary, or unexplained mutations were found.
